problems.quote: `SectionStorage.readColumn` stores `Optional.empty()` for every section of a POI column that is missing, unreadable or fails to parse — `tryRead` swallows an `IOException` into exactly that — and 1.21.1 never evicts the entry, so one bad read stays bad for the rest of the session.
problems.issue: The eviction claim is false on the platform this mod actually runs on. NeoForge patches SectionStorage with `public void remove(long sectionPosAsLong)` (comment: "Neo: Removes the data for the given chunk position. See PR #937") and calls it from `CommonHooks.onChunkUnload(PoiManager, ChunkAccess)`, which `ChunkMap` invokes "for all chunk unloading" (ChunkMap.java:549) — it flushes the column and then removes every section key of that chunk from the cache. The Neo patch exists precisely to fix the leak the sentence describes as unfixed. Verified in both neoforge-21.1.248 sources and the decompiled tree the project builds against. (In *pure* vanilla 1.21.1 the sentence is true — but the page describes a NeoForge mod's runtime.) On top of that, when the chunk does load, `PoiManager.checkConsistencyWithBlocks` rebuilds the section from the real blocks via `getOrCreate`, so a cached empty is not permanent either way.
problems.correction: Drop the permanence claim, or scope it honestly: "vanilla 1.21.1 has no eviction at all; NeoForge adds one, but it only fires when the chunk is loaded and unloaded again — a column that is never loaded keeps its empty entry." The load-bearing part of the argument (one failed or missing read is enough to clear the binding on the very next tick) stands without it.

problems.quote: **Testing.** This repo has no unit tests, and Quark and Sable are `compileOnly` with no `localRuntime`, so parts B and D cannot be exercised in `runClient` — they need the deployed jar in a real 1.21.1 instance with those mods present.
problems.issue: Wrong about Sable. build.gradle:139-147 declares `compileOnly sableJars` AND `localRuntime sableJars` for `libs/sable-neoforge-*.jar` / `sable-companion-*.jar`, and both jars are present in `libs/` (sable-neoforge-1.21.1-1.2.2.jar, sable-companion-common-1.21.1-1.6.0.jar), so the `if (!sableJars.isEmpty())` guard fires and Sable IS on the dev runtime classpath. Only Quark/Zeta are deliberately compileOnly-without-localRuntime (build.gradle:152-160, with a comment saying exactly that). The fact sheet also records the localRuntime on Sable. "This repo has no unit tests" is correct (no src/test).
problems.correction: "…Quark is `compileOnly` with no `localRuntime` (build.gradle:152-160), so part D cannot be exercised in `runClient` at all. Sable is on `localRuntime`, but dev runs are blocked for a different reason — `neo_version=21.0.167` against 1.21.1-targeted mods — so part B is verified via the deployed jar too." If the dev-run version gap is the real blocker, name it instead of inventing a missing localRuntime.

problems.quote: `NORTH_DISTANCE` is `4_000_000`. That is north from anywhere in the world to well within a tenth of a degree — a fraction of one of the 32 frames — and stays comfortably inside the ±30 million world border.
problems.issue: The world-border half of the sentence is not true "from anywhere in the world". The target is computed relative to the viewer (`entity.getZ() - NORTH_DISTANCE`), not clamped, so for any viewer north of z ≈ -26,000,000 the target lands outside ±30,000,000 — and for a viewer at the default border edge (z ≈ -29,999,984) it lands at ≈ -33,999,984, past BlockPos's 26-bit range too. Impact is nil: vanilla's `isValidCompassTargetPos` checks only dimension and a 1e-5 self-distance, and the whole path (`Vec3.atCenterOf`, `distToCenterSqr`, Sable's and Quark's variants) never packs the BlockPos to a long, so nothing wraps and the needle still points north. The angular claim is fine and in fact understated — the only offset is the `BlockPos.containing` floor on X, ≤0.5 blocks over 4,000,000, i.e. ~1e-5 degrees.
problems.correction: Either drop the border clause or qualify it: "the target may fall outside the world border for a viewer in the northernmost four million blocks, which is harmless — vanilla only checks the dimension, and nothing on the path packs the position into a long."

problems.quote: Removes the **recipe only**. The item stays registered, stays in the creative tab and still works; it is merely uncraftable. Only disabling the whole module removes the item — and then existing stacks lose it.
problems.issue: The last clause presents "disable the whole module" as a benign, supported outcome, while the page's own hidden TODO admits the opposite is likely. `CompassOverhaulClientSetup` is an FML-scanned `@EventBusSubscriber(value = Dist.CLIENT, bus = MOD)`, so its `FMLClientSetupEvent` handler runs even for a disabled module, and it calls `CompassOverhaulModule.WORLD_COMPASS.get()` with no gate (CompassOverhaulClientSetup.java:30). A disabled module never reaches `onInitialize` (ModuleManager only initialises modules in `enabledModules`, ModuleManager.java:90-104), so `ITEMS.register(getModEventBus())` never runs and the holder is unbound — and `DeferredHolder.get()` → `value()` throws `NullPointerException("Trying to access unbound value: …")`. So the documented path plausibly kills client setup rather than quietly removing the item. Neither I nor the page has reproduced it, but the visible text states a clean outcome the page privately doubts.
problems.correction: Either caveat it in the visible table ("disabling the whole module is currently untested on a client — `CompassOverhaulClientSetup` is not gated on the module and dereferences the item holder") or fix the gate and then state it. Do not leave the confident version in the table and the doubt in an HTML comment.
